mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate directly reduces the risk-free rate, lowering the discount rate for equity valuation models and increasing the present value of future cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 3.5%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 3.5%, it signals persistent inflationary pressures that prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.5%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous expansion in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong aggregate demand, boosting corporate revenue growth and investor confidence, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (HOUST and RSAFS both above 90th percentile) fails to predict positive returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.05 over 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: In a low unemployment regime (UNRATE < 4.5%), the labor market is tight, supporting wage growth and consumer spending, which drives corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE < 4.5%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Strong payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) indicates a robust labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS growth is above 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 105.0, it signals a contraction in manufacturing and industrial activity, indicating an economic slowdown that reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 105.0, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous acceleration in quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates broad-based economic expansion, which supports corporate earnings and investor confidence, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (GDPC1 growth > 1.5% and HOUST > 2000) fails to predict positive returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.05 over 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: During a Federal Reserve tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising above 3.5% and increasing for 3 consecutive months), higher interest rates reduce corporate borrowing and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods during a tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising above 3.5% for 3 months), or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.
